questions.stem: A block moving on a rough horizontal surface stops after losing its kinetic energy to friction. The same surface is then inclined at 30 degrees and the block is projected up the incline with the same initial speed. conditions: Same pair of surfaces is used.
Initial speed is the same in both trials.
Incline angle is 30 degrees.

answer.summary: Option (C): statement (1) is true and statement (2) is false.
reasoning: On the horizontal surface, the entire initial kinetic energy is dissipated by friction before the block stops.
Going up the incline, part of the initial kinetic energy becomes gravitational potential energy, so friction dissipates less than the full initial kinetic energy.
The coefficient of friction is a property of the contacting surfaces in this model; tilting changes the normal force, not the coefficient.

questions.stem: A projectile is launched from ground at 5sqrt(2) m/s, at 45 degrees from the vertical. At the highest point it splits into two equal masses. One fragment falls vertically to the ground 0.5 s after splitting. The other fragment reaches the ground t seconds after splitting. Find t.
conditions: The split occurs at the apex.
Fragments have equal mass.

reasoning: Resolve the launch: 5√2 m/s at 45° from the vertical gives u_x = u_y = 5 m/s. The apex is at t = u_y/g = 0.5 s, at height H = u_y²/2g = 25/20 = 1.25 m, where the velocity is (5, 0) m/s.
